name: Buen Samaritano, Tegucigalpa, Honduras
region: Buen Samaritano, a community beside the Tegucigalpa dump

families.label: A Buen Samaritano family: the mother picks recyclables at the dump
families.leaveNote: Pickers are no one's employees: 74.8% of work is informal (INE 2024). IHSS pays 66% from day 4, only to contributors.
families.health: At Hospital Escuela, the capital's main public hospital, relatives reported buying their own medicines and surgical supplies (July 2026).

loanOptions.label: A street lender
loanOptions.note: Street lenders charge about 20% a month, collected daily (2022 report; read with care).

loanOptions.label: A bank, if the family has a DNI, a title and provable income
loanOptions.note: Bank loans up to L500,000: 20.11% a year (BCH, June 2026).

loanOptions.label: The relative abroad sends it
loanOptions.note: No interest, as long as the money keeps coming.

families.lifeInsNote: 176 individual life policies per 10,000 adults in Honduras (CNBS 2025).

families.label: A Denver family with a salaried parent
families.leaveNote: Colorado FAMLI: up to 12 paid weeks; about 70% of pay at this salary (90% up to half the state average wage, 50% above).
families.health: Insured through work. Colorado's uninsured rate is 5.9% (2025).
families.loanNote: Average credit-card rate, 21.19% a year (Federal Reserve, Q3 2026).
families.lifeInsNote: 71% of U.S. households earning $150,000+ own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).

families.label: A Denver family whose father does day labor for cash
families.leaveNote: FAMLI needs $2,500 in reported Colorado wages; cash day labor often has none.
families.health: Coverage is uncertain; Denver Health is the city's safety net.
families.loanNote: Colorado caps small loans at 36% a year (Prop 111, 2018).
families.lifeInsNote: 31% of U.S. households earning under $50,000 own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).
